children: Retailers garnered an average growth of 10 per cent year-on-year in August continuing with strong recovery being visible since July, as per the latest estimates released by the Retailers Association of India.
The growth was led by categories such as quick service restaurants and grocery.

The industry body said that the latest Business Survey revealed stable demand trends across key regions and categories as the industry prepares for the upcoming festival season and that it maintains cautious optimisim amidst geopolitical uncertainities.

Retailers witnessed softening of sales growth in April at 7 per cent, which had dipped further to 5 per cent in May. “It has climbed every month since then at 6 per cent in June, 8 per cent in July, and 10 per cent  in August,” the industry body said.

For August 2026, regional sales growth remained consistent across the country at 10 per cent (Pan-India). West India led sales growth at 11 per cent, followed by  South India at 10 per cent, matching the national average.
East India and North India delivered stable growth trajectories during the month, registering 8 per cent  and 9 per cent  year-on-year growth in August respectively.

Kumar Rajagopalan, Executive Director and CEO, Retailers Association of India (RAI), said: “While momentum softened following April, we have seen a clear and encouraging rebound since July. August’s strong performance serves as a promising prelude to the upcoming festive season, and our focus now turns to precise execution and inventory planning to capture seasonal demand. While India’s internal consumption story remains resilient, we maintain a measured and cautious approach in light of broader global macroeconomic conditions.”

In terms of categories, essential and routine categories remained the primary growth drivers, the industry body said. While Quick Service Restaurants (QSR) saw  15 per cent sales growth and Food & Grocery garnered 12 per cent sales growth  in August this compared to same period last year.

Lifestyle segments such as Apparel at 10 per cent  and Footwear 8 per cent  maintained steady expansion, whereas Consumer Durables & Electronics stabilized around 7 per cent following an earlier peak in April, the survuey findings revealed.
While Jewellery segment sales grew by 9 per cent, beauty, wellness and personal care segment recorded sales of 8 per cent. However, furniture and furnishing segment grew by 4 per cent.

Meanwhile, a joint trend report (SANKET) published by RAI and Innoviti, earlier stated that same-store retail spends across India climbed 9.6 per cent year-on-year in August, up from 7.1 per cen t in July.
In terms of same store sales growth, Grocery & General Retail led the field at 9.9 per cent and Fashion & Lifestyle at 8.5 per cent sae the biggest swing of any category this quarter, it noted.

title: Retailers saw steady growth trends in August ahead of festival season: RAI
